content:
Private health insurance for employees is a company-paid programme that gives staff medical services at network clinics, or reimbursement of those services, within the policy limits. It adds to mandatory health insurance. In 2026 a company can deduct the premium it pays, up to MDL 17,400 per employee.

What the employee receives

The company takes out the programme for a group of staff. Each employee gets access to the included services, usually through a card or an identification code, and books an appointment at a clinic in the network. A programme can include:

  • Consultations with a family doctor and with specialists.
  • Laboratory tests.
  • Ultrasound, X-ray and other examinations.
  • Planned or emergency hospital care.
  • As options: dental care, an annual medical check-up or online consultations.

Each service has its own conditions: a maximum amount per year, a number of visits or a share paid by the employee. The offer shows these limits for each package. Law No. 92/2022 on insurance and reinsurance activity places this product in class 2 of its annex, "Health insurance". The National Bank of Moldova supervises the insurance market under Article 4 of the same law.

How it differs from mandatory insurance

QuestionMandatory insurancePrivate insurance
Who organises it?The state system, through the National Health Insurance Company (CNAM)A licensed insurer
Who decides that it applies?Law No. 1585/1998The company
Which services are included?The Single ProgrammeThe services written in the policy
Where can it be used?At providers contracted in the mandatory systemAt network clinics, or through reimbursement if the policy allows it

Article 8(1) of Law No. 1585/1998 on mandatory health insurance provides that the volume of medical services can be extended through voluntary health insurance or direct payments to the provider. A private policy sits on top of the mandatory system and does not replace it, so the company keeps meeting its obligations under mandatory insurance.

How much the company can deduct in 2026

Article 24(20) of the Fiscal Code allows an employer to deduct annual spending on an employee's voluntary health insurance premiums, up to one average monthly salary in the economy, as forecast and approved by the Government, for each employee. For 2026, the Government approved a forecast average monthly salary of MDL 17,400, compared with MDL 16,100 in 2025.

Hypothetical example: a company with 30 employees can deduct at most MDL 522,000 a year (30 x MDL 17,400), if the premium it pays for each employee reaches that amount. If the premium is lower, the deduction follows the amount the company actually paid. The deduction reduces taxable income, so the company's real saving is the tax on that amount, not the whole amount. Any part above the limit and the effect on the employee's taxation are checked with the accountant for each tax year.

What is not usually paid

  • Conditions that existed before the policy started, under the terms of the contract.
  • Cosmetic treatment without a medical reason.
  • Consequences of alcohol or drug use.
  • Experimental treatment.
  • Dental prostheses and implants, unless they are included.
  • Pregnancy and childbirth, in some programmes.
  • Services outside the network, if the policy does not accept them.

Some services have a waiting period from the start of the policy. Its length and the list of exclusions differ from one programme to another, so both are read in the offer before signing.

What the company gains

A medical programme is a benefit that a candidate sees in the job offer and an employee uses in everyday life. For management, its value shows up in three areas:

  • Hiring and keeping people: alongside the salary, the company offers a concrete benefit that can be compared with other offers.
  • Organised access to a doctor: employees book at a network clinic under the policy rules, and included check-ups can be done during the year.
  • A cost fixed by contract: the company knows the annual premium for the insured group, with adjustments as staff join or leave, and the expense can be deducted within the legal limit.

The result depends on how well the programme fits the team. A company with field workers has different needs from an office in Chișinău. The first needs clinics in the districts and suitable opening hours, while the second may care more about annual check-ups and online consultations. Before requesting an offer, the person responsible for staff can run an anonymous survey about useful services, without asking anyone about their health.

How the company chooses the right programme

Price alone does not show whether a programme will be used. Employees value a policy when they can easily reach a nearby clinic and understand what will be paid for them.

What to compareQuestion for the offer
ClinicsDoes the network include clinics in the towns where the team works?
ServicesDoes the programme include the services the team needs?
LimitsWhat is the maximum amount per year and per service?
Payment at the clinicDoes the clinic bill the insurer directly, or does the employee pay and claim reimbursement?
ApprovalWhich services need approval before booking?
FamilyCan a spouse or children be included, and who pays for them?
Staff changesHow do employees join and leave the policy during the year?

Two offers can only be compared fairly on the same services, limits, clinics and people. A lower premium may mean a narrower network or lower limits on the services used most often. At renewal, the company can review aggregated data on the services used during the past year and adjust the package, provided the data cannot identify any individual employee.

What the premium depends on

The insurer sets the premium based on the number of employees, the age of the team, the line of business, the chosen package, the clinics included and, at renewal, how the policy was used in the previous year. That is why no single price applies to every company. An offer can also be built from the budget the company sets aside per employee, including around the tax-deduction limit.

What the company prepares for an offer

  • The number of employees to be included.
  • Age groups or the average age of the team.
  • The towns where employees work.
  • The services wanted and an approximate budget per employee.
  • The previous policy, if there is one.

General information about the team is enough for a first offer. The company does not send diagnoses or other medical data about its employees. If the insurer asks for a health declaration, the employee sends it directly to the insurer. Personal data needed to issue the policy is processed in line with Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection.

How an employee uses the policy

  1. Receives the card or identification details and the list of clinics.
  2. Calls the clinic or the assistance service named in the policy and books an appointment.
  3. Shows the card at the clinic and follows the doctor's recommendation.
  4. If a service needs approval, the clinic or the employee requests it before the service is provided. In a medical emergency the number to call is 112, and the insurer is notified within the period stated in the policy.
  5. If the policy allows reimbursement and the employee paid for a covered service, the employee keeps the documents and submits a claim within the period stated in the policy.

Other insurance for the team

A medical programme does not replace employee accident insurance, which pays for the consequences of an accident. For trips abroad, the option to review is travel medical insurance. Staff packages are presented on the employee benefits page.

Frequently asked questions about employee health insurance

Is private health insurance for employees mandatory?

No. The company decides whether to offer this benefit and which package to choose. Private insurance sits on top of the mandatory health care system and does not replace it. The obligations of the company and its employees under mandatory insurance stay the same, even when the company also pays for a private health programme.

How much of the health premium can the company deduct?

Under Article 24(20) of the Fiscal Code, an employer can deduct voluntary health insurance premiums up to one average monthly salary in the economy for each employee. For 2026, the forecast average salary approved by the Government is MDL 17,400. The exact calculation is checked with the company's accountant.

Can an employee's family members be included?

In many programmes, a spouse or children can be added for an additional premium. The company can pay this part or leave it to the employee. The deduction in the Fiscal Code refers to the employee's premiums, so the treatment of amounts paid for family members is checked separately with the accountant.

Does the policy cover conditions the employee already had?

Conditions that existed before the policy started are usually excluded, limited or accepted after a waiting period. Terms differ from one insurer to another. The company checks this clause in the offer for the whole team, without collecting or sending individual medical data. The exact wording is read in the contract before signing.

How is a new employee added to the policy?

The company usually informs the insurer or the broker, and the new employee joins the programme with a premium calculated for the remaining period. The procedure, deadlines and any waiting periods are set in the contract. When an employee leaves, the company reports the change so that access to services ends correctly.

Does the policy also cover trips abroad?

The programme is usually used at network clinics in Moldova. For illness or accidents while travelling, the company looks at travel medical insurance. Some programmes may have international extensions, and the territory covered is read in the policy before the employee leaves the country.
